name: Meyers OTW / MAC-145
summary: Compact 1930s civilian primary-training biplane built in the late 1930s and 1940s; about 100 were built and survivors still fly at airshows.

wings: Compact, staggered single-bay biplane with fabric-covered wooden wings
engines: Small radial engine (Kinner R-5 or Warner Scarab)

tellTales: Compact tandem open-cockpit biplane with a small radial engine
Short, rounded wings with a single bay of struts
Slim fabric-covered fuselage and fixed tailwheel gear

confusedWith.howToTell: Both are small radial-powered tandem biplanes and easy to confuse; the Meyers is the later, more refined 1930s design while the Fleet has a plainer, usually uncowled-Kinner look.
The Stearman is much larger with a big uncowled radial; the Meyers is a small biplane with a small radial.
The Waco has a wide front cockpit seating two; the Meyers has two narrow tandem cockpits.
